stem: Within what time frame did Kornfeld and Denk (2018) become optimistic that a whole adult mammal or bird brain could be reconstructed from volume EM?
choices: Not before the end of the century
answer: Within the next decade
label: Abstract · outlook

stem: Which methodological combination do the authors single out as a conceptual advance in volume EM acquisition?
choices: Tape collection of sections with multi-beam SEM
Hot-knife sample partitioning with ion milling
Diamond-knife block-face imaging with multi-beam SEM
answer: Hot-knife sample partitioning with ion milling
label: Abstract · conceptual advance

stem: How did the error rate of the best 2018 AI algorithms for tracing neural wiring compare with human tracers?
choices: About the rate of a highly motivated expert
About ten times worse than a novice human
About ten times better than an expert human
About the rate of a moderately motivated human
answer: About the rate of a moderately motivated human
label: Review · AI vs human error rate

stem: How do the errors of different tracing algorithms differ from human tracing errors, according to the review?
choices: Algorithms fail at the same places; human errors are uncorrelated
Human errors cluster at the same places; algorithm errors are random
Both fail at the same hard places in the data set
Algorithm errors are mostly merges; human errors are mostly splits
answer: Algorithms fail at the same places; human errors are uncorrelated
label: Review · correlated errors

stem: Why do the authors conclude that sufficient-quality volume EM data contain all the information needed to extract the circuit diagram?
choices: Different algorithms agree on almost every segmentation decision
Expert humans consistently correct almost all of the algorithms' errors
Redundant algorithm runs converge on the same reconstruction
Ground-truth light microscopy matches the EM traces
answer: Expert humans consistently correct almost all of the algorithms' errors
label: Review · information is present

stem: In the hybrid approach to VEM reconstruction, how is the computer's candidate segmentation tuned before human proofreading?
choices: Few segments split neurites, but many merge neighbouring ones
Each neurite is kept as one segment and only synapses are checked
Few segments merge neurites, but each neurite is split into many
Segments are left unbiased between merges and splits
answer: Few segments merge neurites, but each neurite is split into many
label: Review · over-segmentation

stem: How much human time do both standard proofreading approaches (supervoxel joining and skeleton tracing) consume per millimetre of neurite?
answer: At least about 0.5 h
label: Review · proofreading cost

stem: Why do supervoxel-joining and skeleton-tracing proofreading consume about the same human time?
choices: Both require humans to view every location in the data set
Both rely on the same convolutional network for proposals
Both are bottlenecked by rendering speed of the viewer
Both trace only the centre line of each neurite
answer: Both require humans to view every location in the data set
label: Review · complete-viewing limit

stem: By how much did steering human inspection to ambiguous locations with confidence information reduce proofreading effort in some cases?
choices: Not at all for a fixed reliability
answer: By orders of magnitude
label: Review · targeted proofreading

stem: To what do the authors attribute the recent surge in the efficacy of machine segmentation of VEM data?
choices: A renewed focus on detecting cell boundaries
answer: A renewed focus on detecting cell boundaries
label: Review · segmentation surge

stem: How do flood-filling networks incorporate shape priors into voxel classification?
choices: By agglomerating supervoxels with a trained shape scorer
By hand-designed rules for neurite diameter and straightness
By globally optimising a set of merge decisions
By feeding the previous iteration's in-probability back as input
answer: By feeding the previous iteration's in-probability back as input
label: Review · flood-filling networks

stem: How thin have block-face increments been demonstrated to be with focused-ion-beam SBEM?
answer: As low as 2 nm
label: Review · FIB-SBEM increments

stem: Why can FIB-SBEM achieve lateral resolution almost on par with TEM?
choices: Ion milling leaves a flatter block face than TEM sections
Ion-beam removal tolerates much larger electron exposure
The ion beam itself is used for imaging
Thinner slices reduce electron scattering in the block
answer: Ion-beam removal tolerates much larger electron exposure
label: Review · FIB-SBEM resolution

stem: What do the authors call the one big drawback of FIB-SBEM?
choices: Block-face increments no thinner than 20 nm
Heavy charging under high electron dose
A field of view of only a few tens of microns
Imaging rates far below single-beam SEM
answer: A field of view of only a few tens of microns
label: Review · FIB-SBEM drawback

stem: Into slabs of what thickness can the hot-knife technique cut epoxy-embedded, heavy-metal-stained brain tissue with minimal interface loss?
label: Review · hot-knife slabs

stem: What do the authors expect combining hot-knife slab cutting with FIB-SBEM to remove?
choices: Any loss of material at slab interfaces
answer: Any limit on sample size
label: Review · hot knife + FIB

stem: How long would one single-beam microscope take to acquire FIB-SBEM data for a whole mouse brain?
answer: Thousands of years
label: Review · whole-brain FIB time

stem: Which VEM technique had been used for every whole-brain data set available in 2018?
answer: Serial-section TEM
label: Review · whole-brain track record

stem: Why are serial-section TEM data harder to analyse automatically, according to the review?
choices: Low signal-to-noise from fast camera readout
Missing material at hot-knife slab interfaces
Highly anisotropic resolution and slice-to-slice jitter
answer: Highly anisotropic resolution and slice-to-slice jitter
label: Review · SSTEM drawback

stem: What limits the field of view for TEM imaging of whole-brain sections?
choices: The standard grid's 3 mm outer diameter
The 13 mm width of the electron lens
answer: The standard grid's 3 mm outer diameter
label: Review · TEM grid limit

stem: What net imaging rate does a TEM read out with a camera array (TEMCA) reach?
answer: About 50 MHz
label: Review · TEMCA rate

stem: How do the authors suggest the z-resolution of tape-collected (ATUM) sections could be improved?
choices: Cutting thinner sections with a heated knife
Milling each section with a gas cluster ion beam
Imaging each section at several tilt angles or landing energies
Imaging each section with several parallel beams
answer: Imaging each section at several tilt angles or landing energies
label: Review · ATUM z-resolution

stem: Up to how many parallel beams does the commercial multi-beam scanning electron microscope described in the review use?
label: Review · MSEM beams

stem: With which sample type had the multi-beam SEM been used successfully by 2018?
choices: Sections collected on Kapton tape by ATUM
Sections suspended over TEM grid openings
answer: Sections collected on Kapton tape by ATUM
label: Review · MSEM sample type

stem: Which difficulties stand in the way of combining multi-beam SEM with FIB milling?
choices: Slow material removal and the need for a wide planar surface
Grid-limited field of view and camera readout
answer: Slow material removal and the need for a wide planar surface
label: Review · MSEM + FIB

stem: Which material-removal method do the authors suggest may let multi-beam SEM be combined with block-face imaging?
answer: Gas cluster ion beam milling
label: Review · gas cluster milling

stem: What doubling time did the authors estimate for the number of neurons in imaged connectomic data sets?
answer: About 3.6 years
label: Footnote · doubling time

stem: In which years did the authors' doubling-time extrapolation 'predict' whole-brain data sets for mouse and for human?
answer: 2049 for mouse, 2084 for human
label: Footnote · extrapolated dates

stem: Which principle do the authors invoke when weighing connectomics' biological payoff so far?
answer: Amara's law
label: Conclusion · Amara's law

stem: What neuron count for the adult fruit fly brain did the 2019 corrigendum substitute for the original 250,000?
answer: About 100,000
label: Corrigendum · fly neuron count

stem: Why does the corrigendum caution against the comparison showing flood-filling networks beating a U-Net approach on FIB-25?
choices: The U-Net was evaluated on a different data set
The FFN used extra proofread training data
The FFN result came from an unpublished preprint
The U-Net result was several months older
answer: The U-Net result was several months older
label: Corrigendum · FFN vs U-Net
